text: You're on your phone, ready. Tap an app. You expect it to open instantly, seamlessly. No time to wait.
Most times, it's smooth. But sometimes, a stutter, a pause. Why do some apps leap open, while others drag their digital feet?
You might think it's the app itself, or your phone is old. Perhaps it’s random chance. But a deeper, unseen system is at play.
Your phone's operating system isn't simply waiting. It's constantly tracking: apps you use, their load times, and free resources *right now*.
The OS prioritizes apps it *predicts* will launch fastest, allocating resources before you tap. This creates a bias: fast apps get a head start, seeming quicker still.
So, an app loading instantly isn’t just its own speed. It's the Invisible System guessing your next move, making your digital world feel effortlessly fast. Now you see it.
